note: bytes_per_record is the machine-9 codec payload only (excludes Pebble keys, seqnums, checksums, filters, WAL and LSM overhead; Pebble also snappy-compresses blocks). scan throughput is decoded logical MB/s. The two datasets interleave on even/odd keys so the ingested SSTable overlaps the flushed dataset and the forced compaction rewrites bytes. Automatic compactions are disabled so the forced db.Compact is the only compaction measured. db_bytes_after_compact is measured immediately after db.Compact and may include not-yet-unlinked obsolete inputs; db_bytes_final is measured after db.Close (obsolete inputs unlinked). write_amplification = all SST bytes Pebble wrote (flush+compaction, cumulative) / logical source bytes; write_amplification_stored divides by the machine-9 core bytes handed to Pebble. warm reads use Pebble's default 8 MiB cache; pressure reads reopen the same DB with a 128 KiB cache (working set ~2.5 MB). Latency is single-host and the OS page cache is warm in both read phases. scan and point-read latencies are the median across EKB_RUNS runs (min/max retained); ingest and compaction are one-time wall-clock operations, reported single-shot.

provenance.note: Captured in-container at measure time. /proc/loadavg inside the container is normally the HOST's (containers share the kernel), and Linux counts processes blocked on I/O (I/O-wait) toward load average, so a high loadavg can appear even when the CPU is idle; cpu_idle_pct = (idle+iowait)/total from /proc/stat is recorded alongside so the two can be read together. Each metric's _min is the least-contended run's estimate, and the _min-vs-median gap is the contention signal.
